ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, for the rhombus $ABCD$, if $DB = 10$ and $AB = 13$, then what is the area of the rhombus $ABCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $AC$, intersecting $DB$ at point O, \\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus and $DB=10$,\\
therefore $AC=2OA$, $OB=\frac{1}{2}DB=5$, $AC\perp BD$,\\
since $AB=13$,\\
therefore $OA=\sqrt{AB^{2}-OB^{2}}=12$,\\
thus $AC=24$,\\
then the area of the rhombus $ABCD$ is $\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot DB=\frac{1}{2}\times 24\times 10=\boxed{120}$.
